doc.headline: Keep {arm:September}: at this run's unrecorded provider routing both candidates cost more per reply, and neither is shown to keep Kairo in character better.
doc.lede: At this run's routing {arm:qwen3.8-flash} costs {contrast.qwen3.8-flash.production_replicating_cost.delta|usd_per_1k} more and {arm:1017} {contrast.1017.production_replicating_cost.delta|usd_per_1k} more; both stay within the allowed character loss, so cost alone decides. A recorded routing at which a candidate costs no more would reopen the call.

caveats.label: No provider routing is recorded for any arm
caveats.material_if: Material if a recorded routing puts either candidate at or below {arm:September}'s {cost_per_1k.September|usd_per_1k}: both sit inside the allowed loss, so the call would turn on character alone or become a trade. The earlier round found {arm:qwen3.8-flash} cheaper. Until a re-pricing says otherwise, the measured gap is the only cost evidence, and it favours {arm:September}.

Only if the uncalibrated judge marks the candidates down for replies a calibrated judge would pass, by enough to put one above {arm:September}. The cost gap is measured telemetry, not judged; its own caveat is the routing above.
Only if an aspect chosen before the results would favour a candidate; production cost, which decides, is the same whatever aspect is read.
Only if an arm other than production should be the baseline; both candidates cost more than {arm:September} whichever is called the control.

Only if a setting besides the model moved between arms and moved cost or character with it. Two did or may have: {arm:1017}'s reasoning share differed (Watch), and the simulator's request settings went unrecorded (Method). Either could shift a gap in a direction this run cannot read.

decision.text: Keep {arm:September} (the control) on Kairo. At this run's routing it costs {cost_per_1k.September|usd_per_1k}, less than either candidate, and neither candidate is shown to hold character better.
{arm:qwen3.8-flash}: costs more at this routing and holds character clearly worse, down {aspects.character adherence (v2).reading.qwen3.8-flash.change|abs|pts} points on the pass rate.

{arm:1017}: costs more at this routing and buys nothing for it; its pass-rate drop of {aspects.character adherence (v2).reading.1017.change|abs|pts} points is not told apart from zero, and on holding character alone it is worse.

The cost order contradicts the earlier finding that {arm:qwen3.8-flash} lowers production cost. No routing is recorded here, so the gap may be the provider's, not the model's; the re-pricing below settles it.

The weakest margin is {weakest.arm} on {weakest.criterion}: read on {weakest.interval}, it reaches {weakest.value|pts} against {weakest.threshold|pts}, {weakest.margin|abs|pts} points inside. On the declared {aspects.character adherence (v2).reading.qwen3.8-flash.level} reading its worst drop is {aspects.character adherence (v2).flip_margin.qwen3.8-flash|abs|pts} points. It bears on a rejected arm.

{arm:1017} spent a different share of its output reasoning ({reasoning_ratio.1017} against {reasoning_ratio.September} for {arm:September}), so its cost and character gaps may partly belong to the reasoning budget, in a direction this run cannot read.

Keep {arm:September} now. In parallel, re-price both candidates at a recorded provider routing, including the one the earlier round found cheaper: a candidate re-enters only if it costs no more than {arm:September}.

claims.text: At this run's unrecorded routing both candidates cost more per reply than {arm:September}: {arm:qwen3.8-flash} by {contrast.qwen3.8-flash.production_replicating_cost.delta|usd_per_1k} and {arm:1017} by {contrast.1017.production_replicating_cost.delta|usd_per_1k}, each interval clear of zero. The gap may belong to the routing rather than the model, which the re-pricing step settles.

evidence.caption: Paired change in production cost against {arm:September}, per 1,000 replies, at the family-corrected {family.level} level. Pairing uses only trials that report a cost, so these gaps differ from the gaps between the options table's means.

claims.text: {arm:qwen3.8-flash} holds character clearly worse than {arm:September}, down {aspects.character adherence (v2).reading.qwen3.8-flash.change|abs|pts} points; {arm:1017} is down {aspects.character adherence (v2).reading.1017.change|abs|pts}, not told apart from it. Both stay inside the allowed {aspects.character adherence (v2).margin|int}-point loss.

evidence.caption: Change in pass rate on character adherence against {arm:September}, in points, with {aspects.character adherence (v2).reading.qwen3.8-flash.level} intervals and the allowed loss marked.
The two judged persona checks, paired against {arm:September} at the family-corrected {family.level} level: both candidates are worse on holding character.

claims.text: Off-lane asks carry about half of each candidate's loss on holding character: {strata.off_lane.loss_share.qwen3.8-flash.persona.holds_character|pct} for {arm:qwen3.8-flash} and {strata.off_lane.loss_share.1017.persona.holds_character|pct} for {arm:1017}.

evidence.caption: Change in holding character against {arm:September} in the six largest slices, in points, uncorrected; read as leads. A slice's share of the loss is its drop times its cases over the arm's whole loss: off-lane asks hold {strata.off_lane.n_cases|int} of {cases|int} cases and have by far the largest drop, so they carry the shares the claim states.

claims.text: The control fails off-lane asks the same way the candidates do: {arm:September} drops character on {count.failures.character adherence (v2).September.off_lane|words} off-lane trials, against {count.failures.character adherence (v2).qwen3.8-flash.off_lane|words} and {count.failures.character adherence (v2).1017.off_lane|words} for the candidates, and on the landlord email both {arm:September} and {arm:qwen3.8-flash} brush off the ask, then answer it.

evidence.caption: Every kept off-lane failure for {arm:September}, {count.examples.character adherence (v2).September.off_lane|words} of {count.failures.character adherence (v2).September.off_lane|words}: the landlord-email and laundry cards brush off the ask and then answer it; the match-score card slips into a customer-service refusal.

The first kept off-lane failure for {arm:qwen3.8-flash}, a sample of {count.failures.character adherence (v2).qwen3.8-flash.off_lane|words}: the same landlord-email case, answered with practical advice after the turn to music.

explore.control: The allowed loss on character adherence
explore.binds: Whether each candidate counts as acceptable on character
explore.outcome: Read on the declared {aspects.character adherence (v2).reading.qwen3.8-flash.level} readings, the pick holds at every allowed loss. {arm:1017} stops counting as acceptable below {aspects.character adherence (v2).flip_margin.1017|abs|pts} points and {arm:qwen3.8-flash} below {aspects.character adherence (v2).flip_margin.qwen3.8-flash|abs|pts}; {arm:September} stays the pick throughout because both cost more at this routing.

method.text: {cases|int} conversations, each run {repeats|int} times per arm: {scoreboard.September.usable|int} usable trials for {arm:September}, {scoreboard.qwen3.8-flash.usable|int} for {arm:qwen3.8-flash} and {scoreboard.1017.usable|int} for {arm:1017}. Intervals are over cases, not trials.

The campaign does not state what makes a trial pass on character adherence; the pass rate is trials marked passed over trials usable. Holding character and keeping the booth offstage are separate judged checks.

Readings against the control are at {aspects.character adherence (v2).reading.qwen3.8-flash.level}. Contrasts are corrected together by Holm's method over {family.family_size|int} comparisons, each interval at {family.level}. The weakest margin is read on the corrected interval, the allowed-loss control on the declared reading.

Every judged figure comes from {judged.persona.holds_character.model}, calibration {judged.persona.holds_character.calibration}, with {judged.persona.holds_character.calibration_ratings|int} human ratings.

Production cost per 1,000 replies, at a provider routing not recorded for any arm. Some trials report no cost ({cost.unreported.September.missing|int} for {arm:September}, {cost.unreported.qwen3.8-flash.missing|int} and {cost.unreported.1017.missing|int} for the candidates). Had each candidate's missing trials cost nothing, their means would still be at least {cost.unreported.qwen3.8-flash.free|usd_per_1k} and {cost.unreported.1017.free|usd_per_1k}. Had {arm:September}'s missing trials each cost its p95 of {measure.production_replicating_cost.September.p95|usd_per_1k}, its mean would be {cost.unreported.September.at_p95|usd_per_1k}, still below both, so the order holds at this routing. The paired gaps use only trials both arms costed.

The floor on {arm:qwen3.8-flash} speaks for the pass rate; the floor on {arm:1017} reads holding character instead. Both held; the page reads the pass rate for the asked aspect and shows holding character separately.
The aspect, the control, the allowed loss and the floor were all set on {late_criteria.set_at}, after the runs.
Input tokens, output tokens and model-call counts were not reported; the simulator's request settings were not recorded on every run, so whether they varied is unknown.

findings.finding: Claim character uses 'holds character' for the pass rate on character adherence. It then says 1017 is 'down 3, not told apart'. But the judged check 'persona holds character' sits in the same block, and there 1017 is -4.7 points (-8.2 to -1.3 at 99.69%), separated and worse, as that block's own caption says. A reader takes the two for one measure, and the sentence then contradicts its own block. Fix: call the 7.6 and 3.0 figures 'the pass rate on character adherence'. Add a sentence on the judged holding-character check: both candidates are separated and worse, qwen3.8-flash -6.0 and 1017 -4.7. The decision block's 'Why not' for qwen3.8-flash should also say 'pass rate' rather than 'holds character'.

The confidence reads High over the unrecorded-routing caveat. That caveat is plausibly material: the page says cost alone decides, and that the earlier round found qwen3.8-flash cheaper. Its clause also contradicts itself, calling this run's gap 'the only cost evidence' while citing that earlier finding. Fix: scope the High to the character readings and to the cost order at this run's routing. Then say it leaves open whether a candidate costs less at a recorded production routing, which the earlier round suggests it may. Otherwise, make the form low.

The first next step says that if a candidate costs no more than September after re-pricing, 'then character decides'. The routing caveat says the call 'would turn on character alone or become a trade'. Under the declared criteria, a cheaper candidate inside the 15-point allowed loss would be the pick: qwen3.8-flash's worst corrected drop is -12.6, and 1017's is -7.4. Say so. If the team would not accept qwen3.8-flash's 7.6-point pass-rate drop at any price, say the allowed loss should be tightened now (qwen3.8-flash stops counting as acceptable below 10.8, 1017 below 5.8). Then a reader knows what a cheaper re-pricing would actually do to the call.

items.name: First screen
items.reason: The headline, decision block and the cost claim make the action clear: keep September, because both candidates cost more (+$0.62 and +$0.49 per 1,000 replies, paired and corrected) and neither holds character better. The main risk is missing from the first screen. Under the declared 15-point allowed loss, both candidates are acceptable on character (pass-rate drops of at most 10.8 and 5.8 points at 95%), so cost alone decides. But no provider is recorded for any arm, and the earlier round found qwen3.8-flash cheaper with high confidence. That conflict is tucked into the end of a margin Watch line about a rejected arm. It is not in the headline, the lede or the confidence line.

items.name: Coherent story
items.reason: The claims follow in order: cost decides, character does not rescue either candidate, off-lane asks carry most of the character loss, and the control fails there too. Each sentence matches its block row by row. The off-lane loss shares (48% and 53%), the off-lane failure counts (39, 64 and 62 trials) and the missing-cost bound in Method ($2.24 and $2.36 against $2.02) all check against the data. One small mismatch: Watch puts qwen3.8-flash's weakest margin at -12.6, 2.4 points inside, using the corrected interval. The 'What you could change' table puts its flip at 10.8, using the declared 95% reading.

items.name: Honest emphasis
items.reason: The candidates' character losses are shown plainly. But the cost finding is framed as solid ('The cost finding, which decides, does not rest on the judge') under a High confidence. Yet it rests on a provider routing the run never recorded, and the earlier round said the opposite for qwen3.8-flash. If routing put a candidate at or below $1.89, the call could flip, because both candidates sit inside the allowed loss.

items.name: Sound elision
items.reason: Nothing left out would change the call. The outcome and transcript scores point the same way as the pass rate. The tool check and failed-reply notices are not separated from zero. Measuring spend includes the judge's and simulator's cost. The p95 cost goes the same way as the mean. Story asks are 10 cases, and their large drop for qwen3.8-flash is on keeping the booth offstage, not on holding character.

items.name: Confounds handled
items.reason: The reasoning-share confound is carried on the cost and character claims, in Watch and in a next step. Three gaps remain. The off_lane claim reads 1017's holding-character contrast (-4.7) without that caveat. The model-confound clause says 'each arm's recorded settings name only its model', while the page itself shows reasoning share moving (55% against 76%) and says the simulator's settings went unrecorded. And unrecorded routing, the confound on the deciding measure, is not in the confidence clauses.

items.name: Actionable next steps
items.reason: Each step names an experiment or a declaration and what it settles: re-price at a recorded routing, match 1017's reasoning budget, add an off-lane directive, calibrate the judge, and declare the criteria before the next run. The first step goes straight at the deciding risk.

items.name: Evidence fits claims
items.reason: The cost forest shows the paired gaps and their intervals. The character forest marks the allowed loss. The off-lane bars show the slice changes the loss shares come from. Two smaller problems. The cost block's paired gaps (+$0.62 and +$0.49) differ from the gaps between the options table's means ($0.54 and $0.52) with no note on why. And the examples caption sets the candidates' failures against the control's 'customer-service refusal', but two of the three kept September off-lane failures also answer a non-music ask.

findings.finding: The confidence reads High, and its clauses say cost decides and 'does not rest on the judge'. But the cost order rests on a provider routing that was never recorded for any arm, and the earlier round found qwen3.8-flash cheaper with high confidence. Both candidates are inside the 15-point allowed loss (at most 10.8 and 5.8 points), so if routing put either at or below September's $1.89, the call could flip. Add a confidence clause for unrecorded routing: what would make it matter (a recorded routing where a candidate costs no more) and why the call holds until then. Qualify the headline and lede to say the costs are at this run's unrecorded routing. Move the conflict with the earlier round out of the margin Watch line into its own Watch item. If the analyst cannot stand behind that, lower the confidence.

The claim ranks the three models by cost with no provider named. The caption and Method do say no provider was recorded, but the claim sentence and the lede rank the models as if the gap were the models' own. Say in the claim sentence that the gap is at an unrecorded routing, so it may belong to the routing rather than the model, and point to the re-pricing next step.

This claim reads 1017's loss on holding character (-4.7 points, corrected), which carries the reasoning-share confound (55% against 76% for September). Neither the claim nor the confidence line carries it. Add the reasoning-ratio caveat to the claim.

The model-confound clause ('each arm's recorded settings name only its model') understates what the page itself shows. 1017's reasoning share differed (55% against 76%), and the simulator's request settings went unrecorded. Reword the clause so it acknowledges both, or point it to the reasoning-share Watch item and the Method note.

Watch gives qwen3.8-flash's weakest margin as the corrected interval reaching -12.6, 2.4 points inside -15. The 'What you could change' table and the declared reading put its flip at 10.8, from the 95% interval. Use one basis in both places, or say which each uses. Also drop the '+' from '+5.8 points' and '+10.8': they are allowed losses, not gains.

The lede and the cost block give paired gaps of +$0.62 and +$0.49, but the options table's means ($2.43 and $2.41 against $1.89) imply $0.54 and $0.52. The two differ because some trials report no cost and only matched cases are paired. Add a short note to the caption so a reader doesn't take the figures for a mistake.

The caption sets the candidates' failures (answering a question the persona should decline) against September's 'customer-service refusal'. But two of September's three kept off-lane failures (the landlord email and the laundry question) also answer a non-music ask. The cards are also only 3 of 39, 64 and 62 failures. Say they are a sample, and don't imply the control fails differently when its kept failures mostly fail the same way.

items.name: First screen
items.reason: The headline, decision block and lead cost claim give the reader the action (keep September), the reason (both candidates cost more at this run's routing, and neither holds character better) and the main risk (routing was never recorded, and the earlier round found qwen3.8-flash cheaper). That risk now has its own Watch item and its own next step. The previous round's must_fix on the headline and lede is resolved: both now say the costs are at this run's unrecorded routing.

items.name: Coherent story
items.reason: Each claim matches its block row by row. In claim cost, the paired gaps +$0.62 and +$0.49 have intervals clear of zero. In claim character, qwen3.8-flash is at -7.6 (-10.8 to -3.4) and 1017 at -3.0 (-5.8 to +1.1), both inside the 15-point margin, and the second block shows 1017 separated worse on holding character (-4.7). The off_lane shares of 48% and 53% match measure_breakdown's loss shares. options_dominance makes September dominant, and the margin sweep holds at every margin, so the call agrees with code's reading.

items.name: Honest emphasis
items.reason: The recommended arm's weak point is in plain view: the confidence line, a Watch item and a next step all say its cost advantage may belong to the routing rather than the model. The candidates' character results are not overstated. 1017's pass-rate drop is called not separated, while its loss on holding character is shown. The weakest-margin Watch line now gives both bases (12.6 corrected, 10.8 declared), which resolves my earlier finding, and the stray plus signs are gone.

items.name: Sound elision
items.reason: Nothing omitted could change the call. qwen3.8-flash's story-slice drop on keeping the booth offstage (53.3% against 93.3%, ten cases) hurts an arm that is already rejected. The tool check and failed-reply notices are not separated. Measuring spend and p95 cost point the same way as production cost: the candidates' p95s are $6.20 and $8.27 against $5.30.

items.name: Confounds handled
items.reason: 1017's reasoning-share difference (55% against 76%) is carried on claims cost, character and off_lane (my earlier should_fix is resolved), with a Watch item and a matched-budget rerun. The model-confound clause now names the reasoning share and the unrecorded simulator settings, which resolves my earlier finding. Unrecorded routing has its own clause, Watch item and re-pricing step.

items.name: Actionable next steps
items.reason: Each step names what it would settle: re-pricing at a recorded routing, with a re-entry rule; a rerun with matched reasoning budgets; judge calibration on off-lane asks; and declaring the criteria and recording routing before the next round. One wording point is noted below: the off-lane directive step reads as if no directive existed.

items.name: Evidence fits claims
items.reason: The cost and character blocks show their claims' own figures, and the cost caption now explains why paired gaps differ from the gaps between means (resolved). Two claims are less clearly served. Claim examples rests on September's landlord-email and laundry failures answering the non-music ask, but its block shows September's match-score card, a different kind of failure. Claim off_lane states a share of the loss (48% and 53%), but its block draws only slice changes, from which a reader cannot get the share.

findings.finding: The claim says September's kept landlord-email and laundry failures answer the non-music ask just as the qwen3.8-flash card does. But the September card in the block is the match-score trial, a customer-service refusal, so the claim's own point is not drawn. Show September's landlord-email failure in its place: the judge's reason is 'supplies a suggested opening for the landlord email'. That puts it directly beside qwen3.8-flash's landlord-email card. Then update the caption so it no longer sets September's card apart as a different failure.

The sentence states shares of the holding-character loss (48% for qwen3.8-flash, 53% for 1017), but the block draws only each slice's change (-22.9 and -20.2 points on off-lane asks). A reader can't get the share without the case weights and the overall loss. Add the loss share per slice to the block (strata.off_lane.loss_share.*), or say in the caption how the share follows from the drawn changes.

Method, cost basis: 'had its own missing trials cost its p95 ($2.02 per 1,000 replies)' reads as if September's p95 were $2.02. September's p95 is $5.30 per 1,000 replies, and $2.02 is its mean if its 33 missing trials cost that p95. Reword it, for example: 'had its missing trials each cost its p95 of $5.30, its mean would be $2.02, still below the candidates' floors of $2.24 and $2.36'.

The third next step says 'Add an off-lane directive'. But the run already used the promoted directives, and the judge's reasons cite a 'directive to brush off non-music asks'. The kept failures brush off the ask and then answer it anyway (laundry 'Cold', the landlord-email opener). Reword the step as tightening the existing brush-off directive so it forbids answering after the brush-off, so a reader doesn't think no directive was in place.

Because the page says plainly that routing went unrecorded for every arm, it addresses the cost_served_by fact as far as the data allows.

A cheaper candidate inside the 15-point allowed loss would be picked under the declared criteria. The High isn't scoped to what it covers.

items.name: Sound elision
items.reason: None of the omitted items would change the decision. The outcome and transcript scores point the same way as the pass rate. The tool check and failed-reply notices are not separated. The p95 cost points the same way: $5.30 for September against $6.20 and $8.27 for the candidates. Measuring spend is not what a deployment pays. The story slice is 10 cases.
